goal: Stop the four content workflows from resolving their push target to main when dispatched from main, so they fail before doing work rather than at push time.
non_goals: Changing what the content workflows generate or publish
Adding a pull-request trigger to any content workflow
Touching Gate 3, Supabase, or the roadmap/needs-testing sync workflows
Making native-gate or any other check required — that is a repository settings change
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four workflows refuses to run when github.ref is refs/heads/main, with an error naming the alternative
The refusal happens before any generation or commit step does work
workflow-authority.test.mjs still pins the set of dynamic writers at exactly these four
docs/AUTOMATION-AUTHORITY.md no longer describes their post-ruleset failure as accepted temporary behaviour
stop_conditions: A workflow turns out to depend on committing to main as its designed output — report rather than redesign it
The fix would require adding a pull-request trigger, which is a separate cost decision
Any change would touch a Gate 3 workflow
notes: Identified during the PR3 native-tier audit. These push HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME} or a bare git push, so main is the Actions UI default target; the main ruleset now rejects that at the server, after the job has already done its work. Risk r3: this changes CI/workflow authority, which is r3 by the control-plane model even though production_effect is none.
